page: Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-3840s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 24 dedicated vCPUs spanning 12 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz, supporting two threads per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory allocation provides 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Storage is bundled directly via 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, and one complimentary public IPv4 address is included. There are no discrete GPU accelerators on this instance.

Benchmark tests indicate robust raw compute and throughput capabilities. Multi-core compute performance sits in the top 25% with a stress-ng multi-core score of 67,368.14 and a PassMark CPU score of 51,919.27. Uncached memory bandwidth represents a major strength, registering in the top 10% tier at 458.63 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 223.24 GB/sec for write operations. Conversely, general instruction processing aligns with midrange expectations: Geekbench returns 1,341.0 for single-core and 11,893.0 for multi-core, while PassMark database operations record 11,227.85. Redis SET operations average 54.61 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput measures 19.47 GB/sec.

Instruction set support includes AES cryptography, SHA extensions, AVX, and FMA, though AVX-512 extensions and AMX matrix accelerators are absent. This absence limits extreme vectorization and deep learning acceleration, where CPU-based inference yields moderate speeds such as 26.76 tokens per second during medium 7B model text generation.

With a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and expansive 3.8 TB local NVMe storage, this instance provides cost-effective density for memory-bound and storage-heavy workloads without requiring dedicated storage attachments. It is particularly matched for in-memory caching systems, large relational databases, data warehousing, high-throughput web backends, and multi-threaded continuous integration and build pipelines.
